label: N1QL() function call (from a JavaScript UDF)
type: the N1QL(stmt, params, opts) call form for running SQL++ from inside a JavaScript UDF - supports both named and positional parameters, unlike js-udf:inline-statement-call. NOT the same concept as the already-promoted eventing:n1ql-function-call: both are the SQL++ N1QL() built-in, but invoked from two different JavaScript runtimes (a JS UDF vs. an Eventing handler) with different available parameter/feature support - the source page itself flags 'changes available parameter support' as part of this concept's own label, meaning the two runtimes are NOT drop-in equivalents. Do not merge without a source page stating the two are the same.
recurrence_note: 2 files, `divergent`, exactly at the promotion bar.
evidence: Calling SQL++ from the N1QL() function supports both named and positional parameters.
To execute a SQL++ statement from a JavaScript function, you must have the correct permissions on your account to perform actions on any objects referenced in the SQL++ statement.
relates_to_competency_question: Can a JavaScript UDF call back into SQL++ using the same N1QL() form Eventing handlers use, or is it a separate mechanism?
